header.tagline: Free image upscaler · Real-ESRGAN, HAT, SPAN
help.advanced.p1: Device picks GPU (CUDA) or CPU. Tile size is how much of the image the model sees at once: lower it if the GPU runs out of memory. Overlap blends neighbouring tiles to hide seams. fp16 halves GPU memory use and speeds up CUDA runs at a tiny cost in precision.
help.advanced.title: Advanced
help.batch.p1: With two or more images a strip appears above the canvas. Click a thumbnail to preview it, ✕ to remove it. Upscale runs the whole queue in order and each thumbnail shows its progress. Download all saves every result.
help.batch.title: Batch
help.canvas.p1: Drop one or more images on the canvas or use Choose files. PNG, JPG, WebP, TIFF, BMP, TGA, PSD, PSB and JPEG 2000 work; transparency is kept. Add several to run them as a batch with the same settings.
help.canvas.p2: Scroll to zoom. Hold Shift and drag, or use the Pan tool, to move around. After a run, drag the divider to compare original and result.
help.canvas.title: Adding images
help.filters.p1: On the Scale tab, filters clean the image before the model sees it (Before) or adjust the result (After). Denoise, JPEG clean and Deblur help soft or compressed sources. After: edge enhance, halo reduce, color/contrast, and film grain. Each filter has its own amount.
help.filters.p2: Test compare does not run filter variants. Set filters on Scale after you pick a model, then judge the full-image result.
help.filters.title: Filters
help.missing: Load an image first to see this part highlighted.
help.model.p1: On the Scale tab choose Neural model or Classical. Photo models (RealESRGAN_x4plus, UltraSharp, ClearReality) add texture. Anime models keep lines clean. The denoise model (realesr-general-wdn-x4v3) helps with noisy or JPEG-damaged files. SPAN models are very fast; HAT is slow but detailed.
help.model.p2: Open Model library (header Models link, Method button, or Settings) to rename, describe, hide, download, or add weights by URL, path, or file. Prefer .safetensors; .pth files can run code when loaded, so use only trusted sources. OpenModelDB and Hugging Face have many community models.
help.model.title: Choosing a model
help.model_params.p1: Denoise strength (wdn model) sets how much noise is removed. Open Model library to rename, describe, hide, or add weights.
help.model_params.title: Model parameters
help.output.p1: Auto saves PNG and switches to TIFF above 20,000 px. JPEG, EXIF-JPEG (keeps metadata), WebP and JPEG 2000 are smaller but lossy. TIFF supports LZW, Deflate, Zstd, JPEG or none. PSD/PSB save a flattened composite only.
help.output.title: Output format
help.preflight.p1: Shows estimated time and file size and checks that RAM, GPU memory and disk space are enough. TIGHT means close to the limit. NOT ENOUGH blocks the run until you change settings; Run anyway overrides the check.
help.preflight.p2: Estimates come from image size, passes, model and device, and can be off by a third either way.
help.preflight.title: Before you start
help.run.p1: On Scale, press Upscale. On Test, the same button is Find best model and runs the selected compare variants. While a job runs, Pause holds between tiles and keeps progress; Resume continues. Cancel stops the job and discards partial output. Resume interrupted continues a checkpointed job after a restart.
help.run.title: Run, pause, cancel
help.settings.p1: Switch between light and dark themes, choose normal, larger or largest text, and pick English or Polish. Choices are remembered on this device. Simple view versus Advanced view is also remembered for the next visit.
help.settings.title: Settings
help.size.p1: Choose how large the result is: Scale (a multiplier such as 4×), Long edge (the longer side in pixels) or W × H (exact width and height, aspect ratio kept). In a batch, Scale applies one factor to every image, while Long edge and W × H give each image its own factor.
help.size.p2: Models work in fixed 4× steps. Other factors use as many passes as needed, then a final resize to the exact size.
help.size.title: Output size
help.test.p1: Open the Test tab to process only a small square. Choose crop size, place the region on the image, and pick models and/or classical scalers to compare. The crop stays marked on the source while results load.
help.test.p2: Find best model runs those variants. Comparison includes an Original tile; drag any tile to pan all together, scroll a tile to zoom. Use this model applies the winner and returns to Scale.
help.test.title: Test on a crop

models.desc.4x_clearrealityv1: Kim2091 2023 photo model. Cleaner than UltraSharp, less over-sharpening.
models.desc.4x_spanx4_ch48: Official SPAN pretrain 4x (ch48). Very fast, 8.6 MB. Good general-purpose baseline.
models.desc.4x_ultrasharp: Popular community photo model (2022). Strong texture detail, can over-sharpen.
models.desc.4x_ultrasharpv2: Updated UltraSharp (2023). Less ringing, better compression handling.
models.desc.4xnomosuni_span_multijpg: SPAN 4x fine-tuned on NomosUni with multi-JPEG degradation. Good for compressed photos.
models.desc.hat_real_gan_sharper: HAT-L real-world 4x (sharper variant). Transformer SR, high fidelity + detail.
models.desc.realesr_animevideov3: Anime video frames 4x. Temporally consistent, fewer halos than anime_6B.
models.desc.realesr_general_wdn_x4v3: Like general-x4v3 but trained with denoising; good for noisy/compressed input.
models.desc.realesr_general_x4v3: Newer general-purpose model (2022). Lighter than x4plus, less over-sharpening.
models.desc.realesrgan_x4plus: General photorealistic 4x. RRDB-23, strong detail hallucination.
models.desc.realesrgan_x4plus_anime_6b: Anime / illustration 4x. Lighter 6-block RRDB, sharp clean lines.
models.desc.realesrnet_x4plus: Faster/smoother variant of x4plus; less aggressive sharpening.
